source_findings: The WP1207 activation pointer temp file is fsynced and then os.replace activates it; no parent-directory fsync is visible after that replace.
The exact test set covers injected pre-activation failure and process-level readback/reentry cases, not power-loss/storage-crash persistence.
Linux fsync(2) states file fsync does not necessarily persist the containing directory entry; directory fsync is required when that persistence property is demanded.
Python documents os.replace as atomic on POSIX; namespace atomicity and post-crash durability are distinct.

resolution.reason: Current accepted scope is bounded interruption/atomic activation/process-reentry at repository-component scope, not an explicit guarantee that the newest activation survives sudden power/storage failure.
resolution.future_gap: If the final product later requires crash/power-loss durable commit semantics, specify whether old-or-new recovery is acceptable or new-only persistence is required, then add the matching directory/data durability barriers and crash-level acceptance tests.
